reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that prediction market prices reflect informed trader behavior rather than dispersed beliefs. The price-sensitivity regression (β_i) identifies traders whose actions are driven by private information, not noise. This is formalized through a linear model linking final marginal price to offer price. The ΔAUC test evaluates how much new information is added by a trade, using KL divergence to filter out low-impact trades. These primitives form a dual framework: one for detecting signal (informed traders) and another for quantifying its value (information gain). The failure mode occurs when noise traders mimic informed behavior, leading to false positives in β_i estimation. Additionally, the assumption of risk neutrality may fail in real-world settings with bounded rationality or heterogeneous beliefs.
